idiom_name: std::function<bool(T const&)> predicates composed by hand; choose = std::visit over std::variant
implementation_notes: The carrier is std::function<bool(T const&)> (or a generic lambda kept as a template while it is composed), contramap is a capturing lambda or std::bind_front, negation is std::not_fn, divide and conquer are free functions that combine two verdicts with &&, and choose is std::visit over a std::variant with the usual overloads helper - C++ supplies the dispatch machinery but no validator typeclass, so the combinator set is hand-written. Erase into std::function only at the API boundary; keep predicates as templates inside the rule set.
pitfalls: Type-erasing predicates into std::function allocates and blocks inlining; compose as templates or generic lambdas and erase once at the API boundary.
std::visit requires every alternative to be handled and takes the common type of all branch results: a branch returning void silently throws the verdict away.
Capturing a reference to a temporary (or to this) inside a predicate creates a dangling reference as soon as the composed validator outlives the expression.

variants.name: Concept-constrained predicate templates (C++20)
variants.implementation_notes: With C++20 the same structure is expressed statically: constrain a composition helper on std::predicate<F, T const&> and fold over the rule pack so the whole rule set monomorphises to straight-line code with no wrapper allocation and no indirect call - divide and conquer fused at compile time. Choose it for hot paths and fixed rule sets; the runtime-dispatch variant stays better when rules are data (configuration, plugin, user input) or when the input is a closed sum type whose branches must dispatch dynamically.
pitfalls: Concept diagnostics are reported at the composition site: an unconstrained lambda inside the pack fails the std::predicate check with a long error naming the concept, so constrain the helper rather than every call.
Folding with && short-circuits and collects no reason; keep this variant for pure accept/reject predicates and switch to an accumulating verdict type as soon as errors must be reported.
